why: Wiring cycle 1 (docs/v3/cycles/wiring-1.md, P1 wiring-1.5): a client `DataTable` with `entity`, `money`, `status` and `date` columns at 390 px (a 374 px container) renders as a table, not cards; the Customer cell is 14 px wide and its text invisible while the other three keep 120 px each (`.evidence/cycle-wiring-1/p1.log`, `shots/orders--*--390x844.png`). The row's name is the one cell a phone reader needs. Neither `docs/data-table.md` nor `docs/use-data-table.md` states the `phone` or `cardsBelow` default, so the author cannot tell whether cards were expected.
what: On a phone a table never hides the row's name: the entity column keeps its content width, or the table projects to cards.
owns: the table layout tests and fixtures
the JSDoc gen-docs reads for `phone` and `cardsBelow`
change: Find why a four-column client table with the default `phone` and `cardsBelow` stays a table in a 374 px container. Either the card projection applies there, or the tier drops lower-priority columns before the entity column shrinks below its content (a minimum width for `entity`). State the defaults in the JSDoc so `docs/use-data-table.md` prints them.
proof: make check; a layout test at 390x844 with the cycle's four columns.
acceptance: At 390x844, the entity cell of the cycle's four-column table is at least as wide as its text (`Wayne Ltd`), as a column or as a card title (layout test)
out_of_scope: Server tables, virtual tables and the table's empty state (v3-wiring-1-api).
